facts.text: Mr Mehmet Erdagöz, a Turkish national, was, at the material time, the owner of a shop in Adana. He now lives in Kars.

anchor.surface_text: 9.  Mr Mehmet Erdagöz, a Turkish national, was, at the material time, the owner of a shop in Adana. He now lives in Kars.

facts.text: On 3 June 1992 a brawl broke out between the applicant and members of his family on one side and a Mr H.A. and his friends on the other. Each lodged complaints accusing the other.

anchor.surface_text: 10.  On 3 June 1992 a brawl broke out between the applicant and members of his family on one side and a Mr H.A. and his friends on the other. After the fight each of the protagonists lodged a complaint accusing the other

facts.text: On 16 June 1992 the public prosecutor’s office charged H.A. and others with armed assault, attempted murder and offences under the Firearms Act. Outcome unknown.

anchor.surface_text: and on 16 June 1992 the public prosecutor’s office charged H.A. and the others with armed assault, attempted murder and offences under the Firearms Act. The outcome of these proceedings is not known.

facts.text: On 16 September 1992 at about 2 a.m., police were informed by anonymous call that stones had been thrown against applicant’s shop and windows smashed.

anchor.surface_text: 11.  On 16 September 1992, at about 2 a.m., the police were informed by an anonymous telephone call to Bağlar police station that stones had been thrown against the applicant’s shop and had smashed the windows.

facts.text: Police arrived half an hour later, before applicant was informed, noted broken windows and made damage assessment report.

anchor.surface_text: The police arrived on the scene half an hour later – before the applicant, who was not on the premises, had even been informed – noted that the windows had been broken and made out a damage assessment report.

facts.text: Later that night at 5.30 a.m., applicant requested Deputy Inspector S.K. to have premises searched again before opening shop, named suspects including H.A., but decided against lodging complaint and left police station.

anchor.surface_text: Later that night, at 5.30 a.m., Mr Erdagöz, having been informed of the incident, unsuccessfully requested Deputy Inspector S.K., of Bağlar police station, to have the premises searched again before he opened the shop. He also named the persons he suspected of the attack, including H.A., but decided against lodging a complaint and left the police station.

facts.text: At 10.45 a.m. same day, after consulting security police, applicant returned to police station, handed over two spent cartridge cases found inside shop, lodged complaint and demanded arrest of H.A.

anchor.surface_text: At 10.45 a.m. on the same day, after consulting the security police, and on their advice, the applicant returned to the police station and handed over two spent cartridge cases which he claimed to have found inside his shop. He also lodged a complaint and demanded the arrest of H.A.

facts.text: Police conducted fresh search at 11.30 a.m., found no bullet marks in shop.

anchor.surface_text: A police squad conducted a fresh search of the scene of the crime. According to the report drawn up at the time, at 11.30 a.m., no bullet marks were found.

facts.text: On 16 March 1993, Adana public prosecutor committed H.A. for trial for threatening use of firearm, criminal damage and offence under Firearms Act.

anchor.surface_text: On 16 March 1993, on account of the events of 16 September 1992, the Adana public prosecutor committed H.A. for trial in the Adana Criminal Court for threatening use of a firearm, criminal damage and an offence under the Firearms Act.

facts.text: On 28 June 1993, Criminal Court acquitted H.A. for lack of sufficient evidence; Court of Cassation upheld judgment on 28 February 1994.

anchor.surface_text: In a judgment of 28 June 1993 the Criminal Court acquitted him for lack of sufficient evidence. The Court of Cassation upheld this judgment on 28 February 1994.

facts.text: Shortly after 11.30 a.m. on 16 September 1992, Chief Inspector Enver Tunç ordered applicant and H.A. transferred to security police headquarters for detailed questioning, suspecting applicant of fabricating evidence.

anchor.surface_text: 14.  Shortly after 11.30 a.m. on 16 September 1992, as a result of the events of the previous night and on account of the conduct of the applicant, who was suspected of fabricating evidence (see paragraphs 11–12 above), Chief Inspector Enver Tunç ordered him to be transferred, together with H.A., who had been arrested in the meantime, to the security police headquarters.

facts.text: Chief Inspector Tunç wrote a covering letter stating applicant had frequently lodged ill-founded complaints against station personnel, had animosity with H.A., abused police and judicial authorities, and that his version of events was probably an invention.

anchor.surface_text: In the covering letter which he sent with the file to the public order branch of the security police, Mr Tunç wrote as follows: “In view of the fact that Mehmet Erdagöz has frequently lodged ill-founded complaints against the station personnel, that there is animosity between him and [H.A.], that he has previously abused the police and the judicial authorities, that the version of the events put forward by Mr Erdagöz, namely an armed attack, is probably an invention

facts.text: Chief Inspector Tunç also stated applicant possessed a registered firearm and may have another unregistered one, had made contradictory statements, and requested checks whether persons were wanted for offences.

anchor.surface_text: that he possesses a registered firearm and may well have another unregistered one and that he has already made several contradictory statements, Mr Erdagöz and [H.A.] have both been transferred to security police headquarters for detailed questioning. I therefore request you to check whether these persons are wanted in connection with an offence

facts.text: On 17 September 1992, chief inspector referred applicant and H.A. to public prosecutor; applicant suspected of falsely reporting a criminal offence.

anchor.surface_text: 15.  In an order of 17 September 1992 the chief inspector referred H.A. and the applicant, who was suspected of falsely reporting a criminal offence, to the public prosecutor’s office.

facts.text: On 17 September 1992, applicant and H.A. appeared before Adana public prosecutor; applicant was released same day at unspecified time.

anchor.surface_text: 16.  On the same day, accompanied by summaries of their interviews prepared by Mr Tunç, the applicant and H.A. appeared before the Adana public prosecutor. Mr Erdagöz was released the same day, at a time which has not been specified.

facts.text: On 17 September 1992, applicant lodged criminal complaint against chief inspector and Deputy Inspector S.K. alleging abuse of authority and ill-treatment during inquiries into 3 June 1992 altercation.

anchor.surface_text: 17.  On 17 September 1992 the applicant lodged a criminal complaint against the chief inspector and Deputy Inspector S.K. with the public prosecutor. He alleged that during the inquiries into the altercation of 3 June 1992 (see paragraph 10 above) the former had abused his authority by drawing up a biased report of the incident. He accused S.K. of inflicting ill-treatment on him when he first went to the police station, at 5.30 a.m., following the events of the night of 15 to 16 September.

facts.text: On 18 September 1992, at police request, applicant had medical examination at social security hospital; provisional report noted superficial grazing on left side of back and bruises and swelling below both knees.

anchor.surface_text: 18.  The next day, at the request of the police, Mr Erdagöz had a medical examination at the social security hospital in Adana. The provisional report, drawn up on the same day, mentions the following injuries: superficial grazing on the left side of the back and bruises and swelling below both knees.

facts.text: On 24 December 1992, doctor from Adana Institute of Forensic Medicine drew up new report confirming findings of 18 September report.

anchor.surface_text: On 24 December 1992 a doctor from the Adana Institute of Forensic Medicine drew up a new report confirming the findings of the report of 18 September.

facts.text: On 29 December 1992, Adana public prosecutor discontinued proceedings, concluding abuse of authority allegation unfounded and no proof injuries resulted from ill-treatment by deputy inspector.

anchor.surface_text: 19.  On 29 December 1992 the Adana public prosecutor, after conducting an investigation, discontinued the proceedings. He concluded that the allegation of abusing authority was unfounded and decided not to pursue the investigation concerning the chief inspector. With regard to the complaint of ill-treatment, he noted: ... there is no conclusive evidence that the lesions noted in the report were the result of blows inflicted by the deputy inspector; there is therefore insufficient evidence to prosecute him.

facts.text: On 27 January 1993, applicant appealed against discontinuation order to President of Tarsus Assize Court; appeal dismissed on 23 February 1993.

anchor.surface_text: 20.  On 27 January 1993 the applicant appealed against the above discontinuation order to the President of the Tarsus Assize Court, who dismissed the appeal on 23 February 1993.

facts.text: On 8 March 1993, applicant petitioned Minister of Justice to lodge appeal in interests of law; on 29 March 1993 Minister refused.

anchor.surface_text: 21.  On 8 March 1993 the applicant petitioned the Minister of Justice to lodge an appeal in the interests of the law. On 29 March 1993 the Minister of Justice refused.

facts.text: During investigation, applicant lodged complaint against chief inspector and policeman A.K. alleging insult and 48-hour police custody despite being complainant.

anchor.surface_text: 22.  During the investigation Mr Erdagöz lodged a complaint against the chief inspector and another policeman, A.K., alleging that they had insulted him and taken him into police custody for forty-eight hours even though he was the complainant.

facts.text: On 6 December 1993, Adana public prosecutor discontinued proceedings against these officers, noting applicant was held for 24 hours, not 48, and no evidence supported defamation allegations.

anchor.surface_text: 23.  On 6 December 1993 the Adana public prosecutor made an order discontinuing the proceedings against these two officers in the following terms: ... Contrary to his allegations, he was not taken into police custody for forty-eight hours but necessarily held for twenty-four hours so that the inquiry could be completed. Moreover, there is no evidence to support the allegations of defamation.

facts.text: On 15 February 1994, applicant appealed against discontinuation order to President of Assize Court, alleging detention lasted two days due to police resentment; appeal dismissed on 7 March 1994.

anchor.surface_text: 24.  On 15 February 1994 the applicant appealed against the above discontinuation order to the President of the Assize Court. He alleged in particular that his detention in police custody had lasted for two days and had been due to the resentment the police felt towards him on account of his previous complaints to the European Commission of Human Rights and the domestic courts. On 7 March 1994 the President of the Tarsus Assize Court dismissed the appeal

facts.text: On 24 June 1994, Minister of Justice refused petition by applicant to lodge appeal in interests of law.

anchor.surface_text: and on 24 June 1994 the Minister of Justice refused a petition in which Mr Erdagöz had asked him to lodge an appeal in the interests of the law.

facts.text: Applicant applied to European Commission of Human Rights on 1 May 1993, complaining of ill-treatment by police and unlawfulness of detention in police custody, relying on Articles 3 and 5 § 1 of Convention.

anchor.surface_text: 29.  The applicant applied to the Commission on 1 May 1993. Relying on Articles 3 and 5 § 1 of the Convention, he complained of ill-treatment allegedly inflicted by police officers and of the unlawfulness of his “detention in police custody”.

facts.text: Commission declared application admissible on 3 April 1995, refused Government’s request for Article 29 application on 14 May 1996, and in report of 23 May 1996 found no violation of Article 3 but violation of Article 5.

anchor.surface_text: 30.  The Commission declared the application (no. 21890/93) admissible on 3 April 1995. On 14 May 1996 it refused the Government’s request for application of Article 29 of the Convention. In its report of 23 May 1996 (Article 31) it expressed the unanimous opinion that there had been no violation of Article 3 of the Convention but a violation of Article 5.

facts.text: Applicant alleged Deputy Inspector S.K. beat and insulted him at Bağlar police station when he first went to complain about attack on his shop, refused to register complaint and drove him out.

anchor.surface_text: 37.  Mr Erdagöz alleged that he had suffered treatment incompatible with Article 3 of the Convention, which provides: “No one shall be subjected to torture or to inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment.” He submitted that, when he first went to Bağlar police station to complain about the attack on his shop, Deputy Inspector S.K. had beaten and insulted him, refused to register his complaint and driven him out of the police station.

facts.text: Applicant applied to security police with complaint against officers, returned on advice of head of security police and handed over two spent cartridge cases as evidence.

anchor.surface_text: He had then applied to the security police, with whom he had lodged a complaint against the officers concerned. Subsequently, on the advice of the head of the security police, he had returned to the police station and handed over two spent cartridge cases as evidence.

facts.text: Medical reports of 18 September and 24 December 1992 constituted irrefutable proof of ill-treatment suffered by applicant, according to applicant.

anchor.surface_text: The medical reports of 18 September and 24 December 1992 constituted irrefutable proof of the ill-treatment he had suffered.

facts.text: Applicant alleged deprivation of liberty from 16 to 17 September 1992 breached Article 5 § 1; claimed detention was not based on reasonable suspicion but on police resentment due to his previous complaints.

anchor.surface_text: 44.  The applicant asserted that the deprivation of his liberty from 16 to 17 September 1992 had breached Article 5 § 1 of the Convention, ... His “detention in police custody” had been prompted not because he was reasonably suspected of having committed an offence but by the resentment towards him of the police officers against whom he had previously lodged complaints.

facts.text: Government submitted applicant’s transfer was to take detailed statement about quarrel with H.A., detention was short and due to suspicion of fabricating evidence, to prevent concealment or fabrication of evidence and further incidents.

anchor.surface_text: 48.  The Government submitted that Mr Erdagöz’s transfer had not been effected for the purpose of detaining him in police custody but in order to take a detailed statement from him about the long-standing quarrel between him and H.A. The very short deprivation of the applicant’s liberty had been the result of his contradictory and indeed criminal behaviour, since he was suspected of attempting to pervert the course of justice by fabricating evidence, these being offences under Articles 266, 283 and 285 of the Criminal Code. This behaviour had obliged the police to conduct further on-the-spot investigations and to transfer the applicant to the security police for questioning. The speed with which the police had reacted was due in particular to the need to prevent the concealment or fabrication of evidence and to avoid the occurrence of any further incidents between the applicant and H.A. in the district concerned.

facts.text: No judicial investigation was opened to examine whether applicant committed offences of fabricating evidence; no explanation why police did not bring applicant before public prosecutor same day instead of holding him in custody from 11.30 a.m. until next day.

anchor.surface_text: 49.  The Commission, pointing out, inter alia, that no judicial investigation had been opened to examine whether the applicant had committed the offences mentioned by the Government, expressed the opinion that he was not “reasonably suspected” of having committed an offence. The Delegate submitted that there was no explanation why, if the police believed that such an offence had been committed, they did not bring Mr Erdagöz before the public prosecutor the same day, instead of holding him in police custody from 11.30 a.m. until some time it has not been possible to determine on the following day.

facts.text: Suspicion against applicant reached required level based on specific facts including applicant’s conduct and nature of offences; deprivation of liberty was to confirm or dispel suspicion of falsely reporting offence and fabricating evidence.

anchor.surface_text: 52.  In the instant case the suspicion reached the required level since it was based on specific facts (see paragraphs 11, 12 and 23 above). These showed that the purpose of the deprivation of liberty was to confirm or dispel the suspicion that the applicant had falsely reported a criminal offence and fabricated evidence.

facts.text: Chief Inspector’s letter of 16 September and order of 17 September 1992 stated applicant was suspected of having committed an offence.

anchor.surface_text: In both his letter of 16 September (see paragraph 14 above) and his order of 17 September 1992 (see paragraph 15 above) the chief inspector stated that the applicant was suspected of having committed an offence.

facts.text: Public prosecutor’s finding of 6 December 1993 was that applicant had been detained for 24 hours so inquiry concerning him could be completed.

anchor.surface_text: Having regard to the applicant’s conduct and the nature of the offences in question, the Court sees no reason to disagree with the public prosecutor’s finding of 6 December 1993 (see paragraph 23 above) that Mr Erdagöz had been detained for twenty-four hours so that the inquiry concerning him could be completed.

anchor.surface_text: The Court reiterates that the establishment and verification of the facts is primarily a matter for the Commission (Articles 28 § 1 and 31 of the Convention).
